title: Variant Arbiter: graduated A/B harness with sequential checks, shadow mirroring, and auto-suspend
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Build a reusable A/B testing harness (the 'Variant Arbiter') for model version rollouts that supports staged exposures, shadow mirroring, automated statistical checks, and auto-suspend/auto-rollback when safety or quality regressions are detected. This is intended to be the default workflow for both Hosted and Dedicated customers and integrated into the Redwood Console rollout UX.

Scope: experiment setup API, exposure schedule DSL, randomized traffic slices (user-consistent hashing), shadow mirroring pipeline, sequential statistical checks (early stop rules), thresholds for rollback, telemetry and dashboards, and runbook updates. Not in scope for this ticket: full analytics ingestion pipeline refactor (tracked separately), deep A/B attribution for multi-touch flows.

Design decisions so far:
- Randomization: use stable hashing on user_id or session_id with fallback to request_id to ensure consistent assignment across retries. Rationale: minimizes contamination and preserves KV cache locality where feasible.
- Sequential testing approach: implement a group-sequential frequentist controller with an O'Brien-Fleming-like alpha spending schedule for primary metrics (latency and model-quality delta). Rationale: gives conservative early stopping while allowing power at later stages. We will expose a Bayesian posterior check as an optional mode for customers who prefer it.
- Exposure profile: canonical stages are shadow -> 0.1% -> 1% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% with configurable hold windows and minimum sample thresholds. Shadow runs mirror requests to the candidate and log structured diffs; they do not affect user responses.
- Auto-suspend & rollback triggers: automated suspend if any of the following occur during a stage: (a) statistically significant degradation in primary metric (alpha-adjusted threshold), (b) error-rate increase > 3x baseline and > 0.1% absolute, (c) latency P95 increase > 50ms AND customer impact flagged as high. When suspended, traffic to candidate is set to 0% and an incident annotation is created in the rollout timeline.
- Safety trade-offs: to reduce false positives we require both statistical signal and a magnitude floor (effect-size gating). We accept increased exposure time (longer holds) as the cost for fewer rollbacks.

Progress and work log:

- 2026-03-05: Draft spec posted: https://confluence.redwood.ai/docs/variant-arbiter-spec. Feedback: Design asks for an in-console timeline visualization; Observability requests additional fields in telemetry for request-level diff tags.
- 2026-03-08: PoC prototype for exposure DSL and hashing landed in internal branch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rollouts/pull/642. Early perf note: shadow mirroring increases p99 tail by ~6ms on staging; Eng will add batching for mirror pipeline.
- 2026-03-11: Statistical plan reviewed with Research (Dr. Simone Leung). Agreed to O'Brien-Fleming alpha spend and a minimum of 1,000 effective samples per stage for low-variance metrics. Action: Research to provide a reference implementation for the stopping rule functions.

Decided: mask hashes and allow 'userless' randomization for regulated deployments. Security action: add KMS encryption option for rollout assignment keys in Private deployments.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Customers/engineers can declare an experiment in Console or via API with exposure stages and primary metrics.
- Stable randomization (user-consistent) and shadow mirroring enabled per experiment.
- Group-sequential controller runs checks after each hold window and emits PASS/FAIL/INCONCLUSIVE.
- Auto-suspend/rollback action executes and records timeline annotations; a manual 'force-continue' option exists and is auditable.
- Dashboards: per-experiment metric time series, stage-level comparisons, and a diff-summary for shadowed requests.

Open trade-offs and risks:
- Latency and cost: shadow mirroring and additional telemetry will increase infra cost. We will surface expected cost delta in the rollout create flow and provide a cheap 'lite' shadow mode (sampled diffs) for cost-sensitive customers.
- Statistical assumptions: traffic non-randomness (e.g., mobile vs web) can bias A/B. We'll recommend cohort-balanced experiments and implement an 'enforce-stratification' option in a follow-up.
- Operational complexity: exposing many knobs risks misuse. Plan to provide sane defaults and 'guided' experiment templates for common patterns.

Next steps (short term):
- 2026-03-15: Eng to iterate on mirror batching PR and add rate limiter for mirror pipeline (owner: Ravi).
- 2026-03-20: Research to merge reference stopping-rule lib into core rollout service (PR link will be added).
- 2026-03-22: Design to ship initial Console mock that shows the staged timeline, auto-suspend banner, and diff viewer (Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/abc123/variant-arbiter).
- 2026-03-30: Internal alpha with two internal teams: Search and Summarization. Collect feedback and incident notes.

Longer roadmap items (post-MVP): stratified sampling, cohort-aware metrics, integration with Optimize (auto-suggestions for exposure cadence and quantization settings), and an SDK-level helper to guarantee consistent assignment for serverless clients.
